paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁמַ֤ע אֶל־הַֽחֻקִּים֙ וְאֶל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָֽנֹכִ֛י מְלַמֵּ֥ד אֶתְכֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֗וּ וּבָאתֶם֙ וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And now, O Yisra'el, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances which I teach you, to do them, that you may live and go in and possess the land which YHWH, the Elohim of your fathers, gives you.

notes.official: *wəʿattâ yiśrāʾēl šəmaʿ* 'And now, O Yisra'el, listen' (ASV 'hearken'; *šəmaʿ* 'listen' as exodus-woh 19:5) marks the turn from the historical review of chs. 1-3 to exhortation. The chapter belongs to Moses' first discourse, which opens at 1:6; under `direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah` vv 1-40 are printed without outer quotation marks, and the narrator's frame resumes at v 41. *ʾel-haḥuqqîm wəʾel-hammišpāṭîm* 'to the statutes and to the ordinances' (ASV), the Deuteronomic pair for the law (vv 1, 5, 8, 14, 45; 1 Kgs 8:58; central `mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant`). *YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăḇōṯêḵem* 'YHWH, the Elohim of your fathers' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`). Names follow `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; 'Moses' (v 41) is the grandfathered exodus-woh form, which the Torah volumes share (Kings 'Moshe').

paragraphs.text: לֹ֣א תֹסִ֗פוּ עַל־הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנֹכִי֙ מְצַוֶּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִגְרְע֖וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁמֹ֗ר אֶת־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: You shall not add to the word which I command you, nor shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of YHWH your Elohim which I command you.

notes.official: *lōʾ ṯōsip̄û ... wəlōʾ ṯiḡrəʿû* 'You shall not add ... nor shall you take away': the canonical formula (13:1 MT), paralleled in ANE treaties and law codes, among them the epilogue of Hammurabi's laws and the succession treaty of Esarhaddon (Weinfeld, *Deuteronomy 1-11*, AB 5, 1991; Tigay, *Deuteronomy*, JPS, 1996).

paragraphs.text: עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הָֽרֹאֹ֔ת אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה בְּבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר כִּ֣י כָל־הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בַֽעַל־פְּע֔וֹר הִשְׁמִיד֛וֹ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Your eyes have seen what YHWH did because of Baal-Pe'or; for every man who followed Baal-Pe'or, YHWH your Elohim has destroyed him from your midst.

notes.official: *bəḇaʿal pəʿôr* 'because of Baal-Pe'or' (ASV Baal-peor): the apostasy at Shittim, Num 25:1-9. 'Baal-' without an apostrophe follows exodus-woh's Baal-Tzefon in compound names (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`); the Kings chapters write 'Ba'al'.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ הַדְּבֵקִ֔ים בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם חַיִּ֥ים כֻּלְּכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: But you who held fast to YHWH your Elohim are alive, every one of you, this day.

notes.official: *haddəḇēqîm baYHWH* 'who held fast to YHWH': *dāḇaq* 'cling', the verb of Gen 2:24, is a covenant term in Deuteronomy (10:20; 11:22; 13:5; 30:20).

paragraphs.text: רְאֵ֣ה ׀ לִמַּ֣דְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֗ם חֻקִּים֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוַּ֖נִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם בָּאִ֥ים שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as YHWH my Elohim commanded me, that you should do so in the midst of the land which you are going in to possess.

notes.official: *rəʾēh limmaḏtî ʾeṯḵem* 'See, I have taught you': *lmd* 'teach' is Deuteronomy's characteristic verb for Moses' role (5:31; 6:1). 'Statutes and ordinances' as v 1.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֮ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֒ כִּ֣י הִ֤וא חָכְמַתְכֶם֙ וּבִ֣ינַתְכֶ֔ם לְעֵינֵ֖י הָעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁמְע֗וּן אֵ֚ת כָּל־הַחֻקִּ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְאָמְר֗וּ רַ֚ק עַם־חָכָ֣ם וְנָב֔וֹן הַגּ֥וֹי הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: Keep them therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who shall hear all these statutes and say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people."

notes.official: *kî hiwʾ ḥoḵmaṯḵem ûḇînaṯḵem* 'for this is your wisdom and your understanding': the law as Israel's wisdom in the eyes of the nations (Weinfeld, *Deuteronomy and the Deuteronomic School*, 1972). *raq ʿam-ḥāḵām wənāḇôn haggôy haggāḏôl hazzeh* 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people' (central `goy-gadol-great-nation-promise-formula`); the saying of the peoples takes double marks inside the unmarked discourse (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֚י מִי־ג֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קְרֹבִ֣ים אֵלָ֑יו כַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּכָּל־קָרְאֵ֖נוּ אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: For what great nation is there that has elohim so near to it, as YHWH our Elohim is whenever we call upon him?

notes.official: *kî mî-ḡôy gāḏôl ʾăšer-lô ʾĕlōhîm qərōḇîm ʾēlāyw* 'For what great nation is there that has elohim so near to it': the comparison 'as YHWH our Elohim is' sets YHWH against the gods of other nations, so *ʾĕlōhîm* is rendered as a class, in lower case. The plural adjective *qərōḇîm* does not decide this by itself, since plural attributives also stand with *ʾĕlōhîm* of YHWH (Deut 5:26 *ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm*; Josh 24:19 *ʾĕlōhîm qədōšîm*; GKC §132h) (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 4; ASV 'a god so nigh'; NJPS 'a god so close'). The verse does not decide whether those gods exist; it sets their distance against YHWH's answer 'whenever we call upon him' (cf. 1 Kgs 18:26-29).

paragraphs.text: וּמִי֙ גּ֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ חֻקִּ֥ים וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֖ים צַדִּיקִ֑ם כְּכֹל֙ הַתּוֹרָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י נֹתֵ֥ן לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And what great nation is there that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

notes.official: *kəḵōl hattôrâ hazzōʾṯ* 'as all this law which I set before you this day': *tôrâ* is the written Deuteronomic law (1:5; 31:9-12), rendered 'law' under the new central `torah-law-instruction-rendering-cross-corpus`, as in Kings. *ḥuqqîm ûmišpāṭîm ṣaddîqim* 'statutes and ordinances so righteous'.

paragraphs.text: רַ֡ק הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֩ וּשְׁמֹ֨ר נַפְשְׁךָ֜ מְאֹ֗ד פֶּן־תִּשְׁכַּ֨ח אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּפֶן־יָס֙וּרוּ֙ מִלְּבָ֣בְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּ֑יךָ וְהוֹדַעְתָּ֥ם לְבָנֶ֖יךָ וְלִבְנֵ֥י בָנֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Only take heed to yourself, and guard yourself diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them known to your children and your children's children —

notes.official: *raq hiššāmer ləḵā ûšəmōr nap̄šəḵā məʾōḏ* 'Only take heed to yourself, and guard yourself diligently' (draft and ASV 'keep thy soul diligently'): the *nep̄eš* is the person himself, and the line renders the reflexive under `nefesh-scope-torah` (NJPS 'take utmost care and watch yourselves scrupulously'). *wəhôḏaʿtām ləḇāneyḵā wəliḇnê ḇāneyḵā* 'but make them known to your children and your children's children': the duty of transmission (6:7, 20-25). The sentence runs on into v 10.

paragraphs.text: י֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָמַ֜דְתָּ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ בֶּאֱמֹ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הַקְהֶל־לִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאַשְׁמִעֵ֖ם אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִלְמְד֜וּן לְיִרְאָ֣ה אֹתִ֗י כָּל־הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֤ם חַיִּים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם יְלַמֵּדֽוּן׃

i18n.en: the day that you stood before YHWH your Elohim at Horeb, when YHWH said to me, "Assemble the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children."

notes.official: *yôm ʾăšer ʿāmaḏtā lip̄nê YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā bəḥōrēḇ* 'the day that you stood before YHWH your Elohim at Horeb': Deuteronomy's name for the mountain of Ex 19 (central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`). *kol-hayyāmîm ʾăšer hēm ḥayyîm ʿal-hāʾăḏāmâ* 'all the days that they live upon the earth' (ASV): *ʾăḏāmâ* in the idiom for a lifetime on the inhabited earth (`adamah-earth-land-ground-scope-torah`). YHWH's words to Moses take double marks inside the unmarked discourse (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקְרְב֥וּן וַתַּֽעַמְד֖וּן תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר וְהָהָ֞ר בֹּעֵ֤ר בָּאֵשׁ֙ עַד־לֵ֣ב הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם חֹ֖שֶׁךְ עָנָ֥ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃

i18n.en: And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the skies, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

notes.official: *wəhāhār bōʿēr bāʾēš ʿaḏ-lēḇ haššāmayim* 'and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the skies' (ASV 'unto the heart of heaven'): the physical sky, 'skies' under the central `shamayim` register rule. *ḥōšeḵ ʿānān waʿărāp̄el* 'darkness, cloud, and thick darkness' (central `arafel-thick-darkness-divine-presence-cross-corpus`, whose wohChoice names this verse); the ASV supplies 'with', and so does the line. The description recalls Ex 19:16-18 and 20:18 MT.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֵ֑שׁ ק֤וֹל דְּבָרִים֙ אַתֶּ֣ם שֹׁמְעִ֔ים וּתְמוּנָ֛ה אֵינְכֶ֥ם רֹאִ֖ים זוּלָתִ֥י קֽוֹל׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to you out of the midst of the fire; you heard the sound of words, but you saw no likeness; there was only a voice.

notes.official: *qôl dəḇārîm ʾattem šōməʿîm ûṯəmûnâ ʾênḵem rōʾîm zûlāṯî qôl* 'you heard the sound of words, but you saw no likeness; there was only a voice': the ground of the image prohibition that follows (vv 15-18). *təmûnâ* 'likeness' follows the central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus` (as exodus-woh 20:4; ASV 'form'). For the verbless *zûlāṯî qôl* the ASV supplies '[ye heard]'; the line has 'there was only a voice'. The verse stands in tension with Ex 24:10-11 ('they saw the Elohim of Yisra'el') and Num 12:8 (Moses beholds *təmûnaṯ YHWH*), and Deuteronomy's emphasis on hearing is often read as a deliberate correction (Weinfeld 1972; Mettinger, *No Graven Image?*, 1995).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד לָכֶ֜ם אֶת־בְּרִית֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת עֲשֶׂ֖רֶת הַדְּבָרִ֑ים וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֔ם עַל־שְׁנֵ֖י לֻח֥וֹת אֲבָנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, the ten words; and he wrote them upon two tablets of stone.

notes.official: *ʿăśereṯ haddəḇārîm* 'the ten words' (draft and ASV 'the ten commandments'): the Hebrew is 'words', the source of 'Decalogue', and the corpus already names the units of Ex 20 'First Word' to 'Tenth Word' (central `aseret-ha-dvarim-decalogue-enumeration-jewish-vs-augustinian-orthodox-cross-corpus`, extended to this phrase in the wave diff; NJPS 'the Ten Commandments', with a note 'Heb. words'). The phrase recurs at Deut 10:4 and Ex 34:28. *šənê luḥôṯ ʾăḇānîm* 'two tablets of stone', as 1-kings-woh 8:9.

paragraphs.text: וְאֹתִ֞י צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לְלַמֵּ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֔ם חֻקִּ֖ים וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֑ים לַעֲשֹׂתְכֶ֣ם אֹתָ֔ם בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land which you are crossing over to possess.

notes.official: Moses' role as mediator (5:23-31): the ten words are spoken to all (v 13), the statutes and ordinances taught through Moses (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֥ם מְאֹ֖ד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֤א רְאִיתֶם֙ כָּל־תְּמוּנָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֲלֵיכֶ֛ם בְּחֹרֵ֖ב מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: Take therefore good heed to yourselves — for you saw no likeness of any kind on the day that YHWH spoke to you at Horeb out of the midst of the fire —

notes.official: *wənišmartem məʾōḏ lənap̄šōṯêḵem* 'Take therefore good heed to yourselves' (ASV), with the *nep̄eš* as a reflexive (`nefesh-scope-torah`). *kî lōʾ rəʾîṯem kol-təmûnâ* 'for you saw no likeness of any kind' (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`; Horeb, central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`). The parenthesis gives the reason for the warning of vv 16-19.

paragraphs.text: פֶּ֨ן־תַּשְׁחִת֔וּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֥ם לָכֶ֛ם פֶּ֖סֶל תְּמוּנַ֣ת כָּל־סָ֑מֶל תַּבְנִ֥ית זָכָ֖ר א֥וֹ נְקֵבָֽה׃

i18n.en: lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of any figure, the pattern of male or female,

notes.official: *pen-tašḥiṯûn waʿăśîṯem lāḵem pesel təmûnaṯ kol-sāmel taḇnîṯ zāḵār ʾô nəqēḇâ* 'lest you act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of any figure, the pattern of male or female'. Three nouns of form: *təmûnâ* 'likeness' (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`), *semel* 'figure' (ASV; cf. Ezek 8:3, 5; Phoenician *sml* 'statue'), and *taḇnîṯ* 'pattern' (draft 'form'; ASV 'likeness'), rendered as at Ex 25:9, 40 under the new central `tabnit-pattern-model-cross-corpus`. The noun occurs five times in vv 16-18, and Ezek 8:10 (*kol-taḇnîṯ remeś ûḇəhēmâ* 'every pattern of creeping thing and beast') takes up this very list; one English word keeps that allusion visible.

paragraphs.text: תַּבְנִ֕ית כָּל־בְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ תַּבְנִית֙ כָּל־צִפּ֣וֹר כָּנָ֔ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּע֖וּף בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: the pattern of any beast that is on the earth, the pattern of any winged bird that flies in the skies,

notes.official: *taḇnîṯ kol-bəhēmâ ʾăšer bāʾāreṣ taḇnîṯ kol-ṣippôr kānāp̄ ʾăšer tāʿûp̄ baššāmāyim* 'the pattern of any beast that is on the earth, the pattern of any winged bird that flies in the skies' (central `tabnit-pattern-model-cross-corpus`). The list of vv 16-19 runs through the order of creation in Gen 1 in reverse, from humans to the heavenly bodies (Fishbane, *Biblical Interpretation in Ancient Israel*, 1985). *ʾereṣ* 'earth' in the cosmic triad of sky, earth and waters (central `eretz`, whose cosmic clause is added in this wave; exodus-woh 20:4); *šāmayim* 'skies' for the birds' sky (central `shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: תַּבְנִ֕ית כָּל־רֹמֵ֖שׂ בָּאֲדָמָ֑ה תַּבְנִ֛ית כָּל־דָּגָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בַּמַּ֖יִם מִתַּ֥חַת לָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: the pattern of anything that creeps on the ground, the pattern of any fish that is in the water beneath the earth;

notes.official: *taḇnîṯ kol-rōmēś bāʾăḏāmâ* 'the pattern of anything that creeps on the ground' (central `tabnit-pattern-model-cross-corpus`): *ʾăḏāmâ* is the physical ground (`adamah-earth-land-ground-scope-torah`; central `adam-adamah`). *bammayim mittaḥaṯ lāʾāreṣ* 'in the water beneath the earth', the waters below the land surface, as exodus-woh 20:4 (central `eretz`, cosmic clause).

paragraphs.text: וּפֶן־תִּשָּׂ֨א עֵינֶ֜יךָ הַשָּׁמַ֗יְמָה וְֽ֠רָאִיתָ אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ וְאֶת־הַיָּרֵ֜חַ וְאֶת־הַכּֽוֹכָבִ֗ים כֹּ֚ל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנִדַּחְתָּ֛ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם וַעֲבַדְתָּ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָלַ֜ק יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֹתָ֔ם לְכֹל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: and lest you lift up your eyes to the skies and see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them, which YHWH your Elohim has allotted to all the peoples under the whole of the skies.

notes.official:
*ûp̄en-tiśśāʾ ʿêneyḵā haššāmaymâ* 'and lest you lift up your eyes to the skies': the physical sky, 'skies' (central `shamayim`); *kōl ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim* 'all the host of the heavens' under the fixed rendering of the central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus`, whose astral sense names this verse, so the verse has both English words, as the two entries require. *wəniddaḥtā wəhištaḥăwîṯā lāhem waʿăḇaḏtām* 'and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them' (draft and ASV 'worship'): the verb pair of the Decalogue (exodus-woh 20:5 'You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them'), rendered as there under the Torah clause of the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`.

*ʾăšer ḥālaq YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā ʾōṯām ləḵōl hāʿammîm* 'which YHWH your Elohim has allotted to all the peoples': the heavenly bodies are assigned to the other nations as objects of worship, while Yisra'el is YHWH's own portion (v 20; 29:25 MT; 32:8-9 in the Qumran and LXX reading 'according to the number of the sons of God'). The national allotment of divine beings has its closest parallel in the Ugaritic tradition of the seventy sons of ʾIlu (M. S. Smith, *The Origins of Biblical Monotheism*, 2001; Tigay 1996, excursus 'The Worship of Heavenly Bodies').

paragraphs.text: וְאֶתְכֶם֙ לָקַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה וַיּוֹצִ֥א אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִכּ֥וּר הַבַּרְזֶ֖ל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם לִהְי֥וֹת ל֛וֹ לְעַ֥ם נַחֲלָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: But YHWH has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Mitsrayim, to be to him a people of inheritance, as at this day.

notes.official: *mikkûr habbarzel* 'out of the iron furnace': *kûr* is a smelting furnace, an image of the oppression in Mitsrayim (1 Kgs 8:51; Jer 11:4; central `mitsrayim`). *ləʿam naḥălâ* 'a people of inheritance', YHWH's own portion (9:26, 29; 32:9).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיהוָ֥ה הִתְאַנֶּף־בִּ֖י עַל־דִּבְרֵיכֶ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֗ע לְבִלְתִּ֤י עָבְרִי֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וּלְבִלְתִּי־בֹא֙ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH was angry with me on your account, and swore that I should not cross the Yarden, and that I should not go into the good land which YHWH your Elohim gives you for an inheritance;

notes.official: *hiṯʾannep̄-bî ʿal-diḇrêḵem* 'was angry with me on your account', literally 'because of your words' (1:37; 3:26). Yarden (ASV Jordan), as in the Kings chapters.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י מֵת֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֵינֶ֥נִּי עֹבֵ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְאַתֶּם֙ עֹֽבְרִ֔ים וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֕ם אֶת־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

i18n.en: for I must die in this land; I am not crossing the Yarden; but you are crossing over, and you shall possess this good land.

notes.official: *kî ʾānōḵî mēṯ bāʾāreṣ hazzōʾṯ* 'for I must die in this land', i.e. in Transjordan (34:5-6; central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: הִשָּׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁכְּחוּ֙ אֶת־בְּרִ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖ת עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם לָכֶ֥ם פֶּ֙סֶל֙ תְּמ֣וּנַת כֹּ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of YHWH your Elohim, which he cut with you, and make for yourselves a carved image, the likeness of anything, which YHWH your Elohim has forbidden you.

notes.official: *ʾăšer kāraṯ ʿimmāḵem* 'which he cut with you' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`, whose appliesTo already lists this verse as DEUT-4:23). *pesel təmûnaṯ kōl* 'a carved image, the likeness of anything' (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֵ֥שׁ אֹכְלָ֖ה ה֑וּא אֵ֖ל קַנָּֽא׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For YHWH your Elohim is a devouring fire, a jealous El.

notes.official: *kî YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā ʾēš ʾōḵəlâ hûʾ ʾēl qannāʾ* 'For YHWH your Elohim is a devouring fire, a jealous El'. *ʾēš ʾōḵəlâ* 'a devouring fire' is the predicate form of the simile of Ex 24:17 (also Deut 9:3; Isa 33:14; Heb 12:29). *ʾēl qannāʾ* 'a jealous El' follows exodus-woh 20:5 (new overlay `el-qanna-el-rachum-bare-el-predicate-deuteronomy`; ASV 'a jealous God'; NJPS 'an impassioned God'): *qannāʾ* is the exclusive claim of a covenant partner, and the verse grounds the image prohibition in it.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־תוֹלִ֤יד בָּנִים֙ וּבְנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְנוֹשַׁנְתֶּ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁחַתֶּ֗ם וַעֲשִׂ֤יתֶם פֶּ֙סֶל֙ תְּמ֣וּנַת כֹּ֔ל וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֥ם הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: When you beget children and children's children, and you have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image, the likeness of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of YHWH your Elohim, to provoke him to anger,

notes.official: *kî-ṯôlîḏ bānîm ûḇənê ḇānîm wənôšantem bāʾāreṣ* 'When you beget children and children's children, and you have grown old in the land': a look ahead to apostasy in later generations. *ləhaḵʿîsô* 'to provoke him to anger', a Deuteronomistic formula frequent in Kings (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`; `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: הַעִידֹתִי֩ בָכֶ֨ם הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ כִּֽי־אָבֹ֣ד תֹּאבֵדוּן֮ מַהֵר֒ מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם עֹבְרִ֧ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ לֹֽא־תַאֲרִיכֻ֤ן יָמִים֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֥י הִשָּׁמֵ֖ד תִּשָּׁמֵדֽוּן׃

i18n.en: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you this day, that you shall soon utterly perish from the land which you are crossing the Yarden to possess; you shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall be utterly destroyed.

notes.official: *haʿîḏōṯî ḇāḵem hayyôm ʾeṯ-haššāmayim wəʾeṯ-hāʾāreṣ* 'I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you this day': the cosmic pair invoked as witnesses, in the place the gods occupy in ANE treaties (30:19; 31:28; 32:1; Isa 1:2; Hillers, *Treaty-Curses and the Old Testament Prophets*, 1964; Weinfeld 1972). The pair is the cosmic whole, neither the physical sky nor YHWH's dwelling, and the line uses exodus-woh's form of the merism ('the heavens and the earth', Ex 20:11), recorded in the central `shamayim` and `eretz` entries. *kî-ʾāḇōḏ tōʾḇēḏûn* 'that you shall utterly perish' and *hiššāmēḏ tiššāmēḏûn* 'you shall be utterly destroyed' use the infinitive absolute for emphasis.

paragraphs.text: וְהֵפִ֧יץ יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַמִּ֑ים וְנִשְׁאַרְתֶּם֙ מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר בַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְנַהֵ֧ג יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations to which YHWH will lead you away.

notes.official: *wəhēp̄îṣ YHWH ʾeṯḵem bāʿammîm* 'And YHWH will scatter you among the peoples': the threat of exile (28:64; Lev 26:33), widely taken as written with the Babylonian exile in view (Levenson, *HTR* 68, 1975; Tigay 1996). *məṯê mispār* 'few in number', literally 'men of number'.

paragraphs.text: וַעֲבַדְתֶּם־שָׁ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֣י אָדָ֑ם עֵ֣ץ וָאֶ֔בֶן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִרְאוּן֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּן וְלֹ֥א יֹֽאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֥א יְרִיחֻֽן׃

i18n.en: And there you shall serve elohim, the work of human hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

notes.official: *waʿăḇaḏtem-šām ʾĕlōhîm maʿăśēh yəḏê ʾāḏām* 'And there you shall serve elohim, the work of human hands': lower-case 'elohim' for the images of other nations (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 3; central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`). The four negations (see, hear, eat, smell) are the standard polemic against idols (Ps 115:4-7; 135:15-17; Isa 44:9-20).

paragraphs.text: וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּמָצָ֑אתָ כִּ֣י תִדְרְשֶׁ֔נּוּ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: But from there you shall seek YHWH your Elohim, and you shall find him, if you search after him with all your heart and with all your being.

notes.official: *kî ṯiḏrəšennû bəḵol-ləḇāḇəḵā ûḇəḵol-nap̄šeḵā* 'if you search after him with all your heart and with all your being' (draft and ASV 'soul'): the Deuteronomic pair of 6:5, rendered 'being' as at 1 Kgs 2:4; 8:48 (`nefesh-scope-torah`). The verse moves from the plural ('you shall seek') to the singular ('you shall find'), as Deuteronomy often does (Tigay 1996).

paragraphs.text: בַּצַּ֣ר לְךָ֔ וּמְצָא֕וּךָ כֹּ֖ל הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בְּאַחֲרִית֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וְשַׁבְתָּ֙ עַד־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: When you are in distress, and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days you shall return to YHWH your Elohim and listen to his voice.

notes.official: *baṣṣar ləḵā* 'When you are in distress' (central `tzarah-distress-tribulation-vocabulary`; ASV 'in tribulation'). *bəʾaḥărîṯ hayyāmîm* 'in the latter days' (central `be-acharit-ha-yamim-latter-days-temporal-eschatological-horizon-cross-corpus`). The athnach falls on *hāʾēlleh* 'these (things)', so in the MT 'in the latter days' opens the second half of the verse and goes with 'you shall return'; the ASV punctuation is ambiguous, and the line follows the accents (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). In Deuteronomy the phrase means 'in the future, in the end', not the end of history (Tigay 1996). *wəšaḇtā ʿaḏ-YHWH* 'you shall return to YHWH', the language of repentance (30:1-10).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל רַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א יַרְפְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א יַשְׁחִיתֶ֑ךָ וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁכַּח֙ אֶת־בְּרִ֣ית אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לָהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: For YHWH your Elohim is a merciful El; he will not fail you, nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which he swore to them.

notes.official: *kî ʾēl raḥûm YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā* 'For YHWH your Elohim is a merciful El' (`el-qanna-el-rachum-bare-el-predicate-deuteronomy`; cf. Ex 34:6). *lōʾ yarpəḵā* 'he will not fail you', literally 'let you drop'. *bərîṯ ʾăḇōṯeyḵā* 'the covenant of your fathers', the oath to the patriarchs.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י שְׁאַל־נָא֩ לְיָמִ֨ים רִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֗יךָ לְמִן־הַיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁר֩ בָּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אָדָם֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְצֵ֥ה הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְעַד־קְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם הֲנִֽהְיָ֗ה כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַגָּדוֹל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה א֖וֹ הֲנִשְׁמַ֥ע כָּמֹֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that the Elohim created humankind upon the earth, and from one end of the skies to the other end of the skies, whether there has been anything like this great thing, or whether anything like it has been heard.

notes.official: *ləmin-hayyôm ʾăšer bārāʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾāḏām ʿal-hāʾāreṣ* 'since the day that the Elohim created humankind upon the earth': an echo of Gen 1:27 (*wayyiḇrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-hāʾāḏām*). *ʾāḏām* without the article is collective, 'humankind', as genesis-woh renders it at 1:26-27 (draft and ASV 'man'; new overlay `bara-elohim-adam-deuteronomy-4-32`). genesis-woh renders the verb *bārāʾ* 'shape' under the central `bara` entry, which is scoped to Gen 1; outside Genesis the corpus renders *bārāʾ* 'create' (ratified at the human sign-off of this wave, 2026-11-01), as here. *ûləmiqṣēh haššāmayim wəʿaḏ-qəṣēh haššāmāyim* 'and from one end of the skies to the other end of the skies': spatial extent, 'skies' under the central `shamayim` (cf. 30:4; Ps 19:7 MT). The questions of vv 32-34 survey all time and all space (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: הֲשָׁ֣מַֽע עָם֩ ק֨וֹל אֱלֹהִ֜ים מְדַבֵּ֧ר מִתּוֹךְ־הָאֵ֛שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֥עְתָּ אַתָּ֖ה וַיֶּֽחִי׃

i18n.en: Did a people ever hear the voice of the Elohim speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?

notes.official: *hăšāmaʿ ʿām qôl ʾĕlōhîm mədabbēr mittôḵ-hāʾēš kaʾăšer-šāmaʿtā ʾattâ wayyeḥî* 'Did a people ever hear the voice of the Elohim speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and live?': the voice is that of the Horeb theophany (vv 12, 36), and the line keeps the YHWH referent of the ASV (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`); NRSV and NJPS read 'the voice of a god'. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the LXX add 'living' (*ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm*), as at 5:26 MT (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). To hear and live answers the fear of Ex 20:16 MT and the principle of Ex 33:20.

paragraphs.text: א֣וֹ ׀ הֲנִסָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֗ים לָ֠בוֹא לָקַ֨חַת ל֣וֹ גוֹי֮ מִקֶּ֣רֶב גּוֹי֒ בְּמַסֹּת֩ בְּאֹתֹ֨ת וּבְמוֹפְתִ֜ים וּבְמִלְחָמָ֗ה וּבְיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבְמוֹרָאִ֖ים גְּדֹלִ֑ים כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֛ם בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Or has any elohim ventured to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that YHWH your Elohim did for you in Mitsrayim before your eyes?

notes.official: *ʾô hănissâ ʾĕlōhîm lāḇôʾ lāqaḥaṯ lô ḡôy miqqereḇ gôy* 'Or has any elohim ventured to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation' (draft 'has the Elohim ventured'): the question measures any other god against 'all that YHWH your Elohim did for you in Mitsrayim', so *ʾĕlōhîm* is the generic class, in lower case (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 4; NRSV 'has any god ever attempted'; NJPS 'has any god ventured'); the ASV 'hath God assayed' takes the YHWH referent. *bəmassōṯ bəʾōṯōṯ ûḇəmôp̄ṯîm ûḇəmilḥāmâ ûḇəyāḏ ḥăzāqâ ûḇizrôaʿ nəṭûyâ ûḇəmôrāʾîm gəḏōlîm* 'by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors': the Deuteronomic formula of the Exodus, here in its fullest form (26:8; 34:11-12; central `mitsrayim`).

paragraphs.text: אַתָּה֙ הָרְאֵ֣תָ לָדַ֔עַת כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד מִלְבַדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: To you it was shown, that you might know that YHWH, he is the Elohim; there is none else besides him.

notes.official: *ʾattâ horʾēṯā lāḏaʿaṯ* 'To you it was shown, that you might know' (Hophal, as Ex 25:40 *morʾeh*). *kî YHWH hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm ʾên ʿôḏ millaḇaddô* 'that YHWH, he is the Elohim; there is none else besides him': the formula of 1 Kgs 18:39 and 8:60. Whether it denies the existence of other gods or YHWH's parity with them is debated, since vv 19 and 28 speak of other objects of worship (MacDonald, *Deuteronomy and the Meaning of 'Monotheism'*, 2003; Smith 2001; central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`); the line renders the Hebrew.

paragraphs.text: מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם הִשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ לְיַסְּרֶ֑ךָּ וְעַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ הֶרְאֲךָ֙ אֶת־אִשּׁ֣וֹ הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּדְבָרָ֥יו שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: Out of the heavens he made you hear his voice, that he might instruct you; and on the earth he made you see his great fire; and you heard his words out of the midst of the fire.

notes.official: *min-haššāmayim hišmîʿăḵā ʾeṯ-qōlô ləyassərekkā* 'Out of the heavens he made you hear his voice, that he might instruct you': *šāmayim* as the realm from which YHWH speaks takes 'heavens' (central `shamayim`, divine-realm register; cf. exodus-woh 20:19 'from the heavens'). *yissēr* is 'discipline, correct, train' (8:5; NRSV 'to discipline you'); the ASV 'instruct' is kept. *wəʿal-hāʾāreṣ herʾăḵā ʾeṯ-ʾiššô haggəḏôlâ* 'and on the earth he made you see his great fire' (central `eretz`, cosmic clause): the verse divides the theophany between heaven (the voice) and earth (the fire), which many read as Deuteronomy's correction of the descent of Ex 19:18, 20 (von Rad, *Studies in Deuteronomy*, 1953; Weinfeld 1972).

paragraphs.text: וְתַ֗חַת כִּ֤י אָהַב֙ אֶת־אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ וַיִּבְחַ֥ר בְּזַרְע֖וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וַיּוֹצִֽאֲךָ֧ בְּפָנָ֛יו בְּכֹח֥וֹ הַגָּדֹ֖ל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And because he loved your fathers, he chose his seed after him, and brought you out with his presence, with his great power, out of Mitsrayim,

notes.official:
*wəṯaḥaṯ kî ʾāhaḇ ʾeṯ-ʾăḇōṯeyḵā wayyiḇḥar bəzarʿô ʾaḥărāyw* 'And because he loved your fathers, he chose his seed after him': the MT has singular suffixes, 'his seed after him', referring distributively to each father or to Avraham; the Samaritan Pentateuch, the LXX, the Peshitta and the Vulgate have 'their seed after them', and the ASV follows them. The line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`; Driver, *Deuteronomy*, ICC, 1895; Tigay 1996). *bāḥar* 'choose' is Deuteronomy's verb of election (7:6-8; 10:15). *wayyôṣiʾăḵā bəp̄ānāyw* 'and brought you out with his presence', literally 'with his face', i.e. in person (`panim-presence-face-convention-torah`; cf. Ex 33:14; Isa 63:9). *mimmiṣrāyim* 'out of Mitsrayim' (central `mitsrayim`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse in the versional form ('And because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them'; French 'il a choisi leur race après eux') as the conclusion of the chosen people's journey to their promised country. The line keeps the MT 'his seed after him'; the plural of the canon's quotation is that of the Samaritan Pentateuch, the LXX, the KJV and the ASV, recorded above.

paragraphs.text: לְהוֹרִ֗ישׁ גּוֹיִ֛ם גְּדֹלִ֧ים וַעֲצֻמִ֛ים מִמְּךָ֖ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ לַהֲבִֽיאֲךָ֗ לָֽתֶת־לְךָ֧ אֶת־אַרְצָ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: to drive out from before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as at this day.

notes.official: *ləhôrîš gôyim gəḏōlîm waʿăṣumîm mimməḵā mippāneyḵā* 'to drive out from before you nations greater and mightier than you' (7:1; 9:1; 11:23). *kayyôm hazzeh* 'as at this day': for the speaker the Transjordanian lands are already held (2:24-3:17; central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְיָדַעְתָּ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ֮ אֶל־לְבָבֶךָ֒ כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּ֑חַת אֵ֖ין עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: Know therefore this day, and lay it to your heart, that YHWH, he is the Elohim in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is none else.

notes.official: *kî YHWH hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm baššāmayim mimmaʿal wəʿal-hāʾāreṣ mittāḥaṯ ʾên ʿôḏ* 'that YHWH, he is the Elohim in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is none else': the cosmic merism of YHWH's rule ('heavens', central `shamayim`, divine-realm register; 'earth', central `eretz`, cosmic clause), as in Rahab's confession (Josh 2:11) and 1 Kgs 8:23. See v 35 on the debate over monotheism.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֞ אֶת־חֻקָּ֣יו וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁר֙ יִיטַ֣ב לְךָ֔ וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וּלְמַ֨עַן תַּאֲרִ֤יךְ יָמִים֙ עַל־הַ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And you shall keep his statutes and his commandments which I command you this day, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land which YHWH your Elohim gives you, for all time.

notes.official: *ləmaʿan taʾărîḵ yāmîm ʿal-hāʾăḏāmâ ʾăšer YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā nōṯēn ləḵā* 'that you may prolong your days upon the land which YHWH your Elohim gives you' (draft 'ground'): *ʾăḏāmâ* is the territory given to Yisra'el, rendered 'land' as in the ASV and 1-kings-woh 8:34, 40 (`adamah-earth-land-ground-scope-torah`). *ḥuqqāyw ûmiṣwōṯāyw* 'his statutes and his commandments' (central `mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant`). *kol-hayyāmîm* 'for all time', literally 'all the days'. The verse closes the discourse of 1:6-4:40.

paragraphs.text: אָ֣ז יַבְדִּ֤יל מֹשֶׁה֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ עָרִ֔ים בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִזְרְחָ֖ה שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Yarden, toward the sunrise,

notes.official: *ʾāz yaḇdîl mōšeh šālōš ʿārîm* 'Then Moses set apart three cities': the narrator's frame resumes, without quotation marks (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`). These are the cities of refuge east of the Yarden (Num 35:9-15; Deut 19:1-13; Josh 20). *mizrəḥâ šāmeš* 'toward the sunrise', i.e. eastward.

paragraphs.text: לָנֻ֨ס שָׁ֜מָּה רוֹצֵ֗חַ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְצַ֤ח אֶת־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּבְלִי־דַ֔עַת וְה֛וּא לֹא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ל֖וֹ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשׁ֑וֹם וְנָ֗ס אֶל־אַחַ֛ת מִן־הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖ל וָחָֽי׃

i18n.en: that the manslayer might flee there, who kills his neighbor unawares and did not hate him in time past, and that fleeing to one of these cities he might live:

notes.official: *rôṣēaḥ ʾăšer yirṣaḥ ʾeṯ-rēʿēhû biḇlî-ḏaʿaṯ* 'the manslayer ... who kills his neighbor unawares' (ASV 'slayeth'): the verb of the Decalogue (*lōʾ tirṣāḥ*, exodus-woh 20:13 'murder'), here of a killing without intent, for which 'murder' would be self-contradictory in English; the line keeps the ASV sense (new overlay `rotseach-manslayer-unintentional-killing-deuteronomy-4-42`, which limits the exodus-woh 'murder' entry to the Decalogue). *mittəmôl šilšôm* 'in time past', literally 'yesterday and the day before'. *wāḥāy* 'he might live'.

paragraphs.text: אֶת־בֶּ֧צֶר בַּמִּדְבָּ֛ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֖ר לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִ֑י וְאֶת־רָאמֹ֤ת בַּגִּלְעָד֙ לַגָּדִ֔י וְאֶת־גּוֹלָ֥ן בַּבָּשָׁ֖ן לַֽמְנַשִּֽׁי׃

i18n.en: Betzer in the wilderness, in the plain country, for the Re'uvenites; and Ramot in Gil'ad, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Menashites.

notes.official: Betzer (ASV Bezer) *bəʾereṣ hammîšōr* 'in the plain country', the Moabite plateau (NJPS 'the tableland'; Betzer is also named on the Mesha stele, line 27; central `eretz`). Ramot in Gil'ad (ASV Ramoth in Gilead) and Golan in Bashan. *lārəʾûḇēnî ... laggāḏî ... lamnaššî* 'for the Re'uvenites ... for the Gadites ... for the Menashites' (ASV Reubenites, Manassites): Hebrew collective singulars, rendered as English plurals with '-ite' on the transliterated stem (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְזֹ֖את הַתּוֹרָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And this is the law which Moses set before the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *wəzōʾṯ hattôrâ* 'And this is the law': the heading of the second discourse (4:44-28:68), with *tôrâ* as the written law ('law' under the central `torah-law-instruction-rendering-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: אֵ֚לֶּה הָֽעֵדֹ֔ת וְהַֽחֻקִּ֖ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: These are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which Moses spoke to the children of Yisra'el when they came out of Mitsrayim,

notes.official: *hāʿēḏōṯ wəhaḥuqqîm wəhammišpāṭîm* 'the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances' (ASV; central `mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant`): *ʿēḏōṯ* is the plural legal noun, in lower case; the capitalised 'the Testimony' of Ex 25:16 and Num 18:2 names the tablets. *bəṣēʾṯām mimmiṣrāyim* 'when they came out of Mitsrayim', i.e. in the period after the Exodus (central `mitsrayim`).

paragraphs.text: בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן בַּגַּ֗יְא מ֚וּל בֵּ֣ית פְּע֔וֹר בְּאֶ֗רֶץ סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֤ה מֹשֶׁה֙ וּבְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: beyond the Yarden, in the valley opposite Beit-Pe'or, in the land of Sichon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Cheshbon, whom Moses and the children of Yisra'el struck when they came out of Mitsrayim.

notes.official: *baggayʾ mûl bêṯ pəʿôr* 'in the valley opposite Beit-Pe'or' (ASV Beth-peor; 3:29; 34:6), the camp before the crossing. Sichon and Cheshbon as Num 21:21-26 (central `eretz`; `mitsrayim`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽירְשׁ֨וּ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ וְאֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ ׀ ע֣וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֗ן שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִזְרַ֖ח שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Yarden toward the sunrise;

notes.official: *wayyîrəšû ʾeṯ-ʾarṣô* 'And they took possession of his land': the kingdoms of Sichon and Og, Num 21:21-35; Deut 2:26-3:11 (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֧חַל אַרְנֹ֛ן וְעַד־הַ֥ר שִׂיאֹ֖ן ה֥וּא חֶרְמֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: from Aro'er, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, as far as Mount Si'on — that is Chermon —

notes.official: *mēʿărōʿēr* 'from Aro'er' (ASV Aroer), on the Arnon (2:36; Mesha stele line 26). *wəʿaḏ-har śîʾōn hûʾ ḥermôn* 'as far as Mount Si'on — that is Chermon' (ASV 'mount Sion ... Hermon'): *śîʾōn*, with *śîn*, is distinct from *ṣiyyôn* 'Zion'. The Peshitta reads 'Sirion', the Sidonian name of Hermon given at 3:9, and many commentators emend accordingly; the line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־הָ֨עֲרָבָ֜ה עֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה וְעַ֖ד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֑ה תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: and all the Aravah beyond the Yarden eastward, as far as the Sea of the Aravah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

notes.official: *wəḵol-hāʿărāḇâ* 'and all the Aravah' (ASV Arabah), the rift valley of the Yarden and the Dead Sea; *yam hāʿărāḇâ* 'the Sea of the Aravah' is the Dead Sea (3:17; Josh 3:16). *ʾašdōṯ happisgâ* 'the slopes of Pisgah' (cf. Num 21:15).
